about.title: Orgue Vivant
about.intro: Orgue Vivant is a community initiative to keep organ music alive in downtown Lille. We organise free or low-cost concerts, open to everyone.
about.stMaurice: The grand organ of Saint-Maurice was built in 1877 by the Maison Delmotte of Tournai, housed in a carved oak case crafted in 1878 by Lille cabinetmaker Charles Buisine-Rigot. The instrument underwent a major reconstruction in 1961 by Jean Pascal, who refounded approximately 85% of the organ while preserving the original case. With 48 stops across three manuals and pedal, four Barker machines, and a window console with 12 programmable combinations, it offers an exceptionally rich tonal palette. Its pitch is set at 435 Hz in equal temperament.
about.stEtienne: The gallery organ of Saint-Étienne is one of the most precious instruments in northern France. Built in 1840 by Daublaine-Callinet — a partnership between Louis Callinet and André Marie Daublaine — it was profoundly reworked in 1886 by master builder Aristide Cavaillé-Coll, then again in 1901 by Charles Mutin. Listed as a historical monument since 1980, this 42-stop instrument across three manuals and pedal bears witness to the evolution of French Romantic organ building. With its Barker machine on the Grand-Orgue and a pitch of 440 Hz, it remains a remarkably expressive instrument.
about.mission: Make organ music accessible, support the next generation of organists, and showcase Lille's musical heritage.

privacy.purposesTitle: Data processed, purposes and legal bases
privacy.purposes:
Contact form — Data: name, email address, content of the message. Purpose: replying to requests sent to the association. Legal basis: the association's legitimate interest in replying to those who contact it (Article 6(1)(f) GDPR). The message is forwarded by email to the association.

Newsletter — Data: email address, subscription and confirmation dates. Purpose: communicating concert dates, scheduled artists and festival news. Legal basis: the data subject's consent (Article 6(1)(a) GDPR), given through a subscription confirmed from their mailbox. Consent may be withdrawn at any time via the unsubscribe link in every mailing; the address is then deleted without delay.

Audience measurement — Data: number of visits and pages viewed, measured with Vercel Web Analytics. No cookie or identifier is placed on the user's device; the data is aggregated and cannot track a person across sites. Legal basis: the association's legitimate interest in knowing the Site's audience. This mechanism does not require the user's consent.

Technical logs — Data: IP address and requests, recorded by the host. Purpose: security and proper operation of the Site. Legal basis: legitimate interest.
privacy.processors:
Data is neither sold nor disclosed to third parties for commercial purposes. It is processed on behalf of the association, under a contract compliant with Article 28 GDPR, by the following processors:

– Vercel Inc. (United States) — hosting of the Site and audience measurement
– Supabase Inc. — database, hosted in London (United Kingdom)
– Resend Inc. (United States) — email delivery: newsletter, subscription confirmation, contact form messages
privacy.transfers:
The United Kingdom benefits from an adequacy decision of the European Commission within the meaning of Article 45 GDPR.

Processing carried out in the United States by Vercel Inc. and Resend Inc. is governed by the standard contractual clauses adopted by the European Commission, incorporated in the data processing agreements concluded with these providers, in accordance with Article 46 GDPR.
privacy.retention:
– Contact form messages: one year from the last exchange
– Newsletter: until unsubscription; an unconfirmed subscription is deleted after thirty days
– Audience measurement: aggregated data, no individual identifier
– Technical logs: a few days
privacy.cookies:
The Site only places cookies strictly necessary for its operation, exempt from consent under Article 82 of the French Data Protection Act:

– i18n_redirected: stores the chosen language (duration: one year)
– ov_cookie_consent: records that the cookie information has been read (duration: one year)

No advertising, audience-measurement or tracking cookie is used.
privacy.security: The association implements appropriate technical and organisational measures to ensure the security and confidentiality of data: encryption of communications (HTTPS), restricted access to the database, protection of forms against automated submissions, and reliance on providers offering sufficient guarantees.
privacy.rights:
In accordance with Articles 15 to 22 GDPR, every person has the right to access, rectify and erase their data, the right to restriction of processing, the right to object and the right to data portability, as well as the right to withdraw consent at any time for processing based on it.

These rights may be exercised by email at contact{'@'}orguevivant.fr. The association replies within one month of receiving the request and may, in case of reasonable doubt about the applicant's identity, request supporting evidence.

Anyone who considers that their rights are not respected may lodge a complaint with the French data protection authority, the Commission nationale de l'informatique et des libertés (CNIL), 3 place de Fontenoy, TSA 80715, 75334 Paris Cedex 07, France — www.cnil.fr.
